headline: Dengue cases surpass 1 lakh this year as 4 more die
summary: Bangladesh has recorded over 100,000 dengue cases this year, with four more deaths reported in the last 24 hours. The DGHS confirms 307 fatalities nationwide.
details: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reported that at least four dengue patients died and 2,167 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours until 8:00am today. All four deaths were reported in areas under Dhaka South City Corporation.

With the new fatalities and hospitalisations, the total number of dengue deaths has risen to 307, and the total number of cases has reached 1,01,442. This marks a significant surge in the mosquito-borne disease.
Currently, 5,834 dengue patients are undergoing treatment at various hospitals across the country. Health authorities are urging the public to take preventive measures against mosquito bites.

headline_marked: CUET staff and teachers [[announce work abstention]] demanding new VC's removal
headline: CUET staff and teachers announce work abstention demanding new VC's removal
summary: Protests intensify at Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology as teachers and staff demand the reinstatement of the former Vice-Chancellor.
details: Teachers, officers, and staff of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) have announced a complete work abstention and all-out non-cooperation to demand the removal of newly appointed Vice-Chancellor Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam.
The decision was announced by CUET Teachers’ Association President Professor Mohammad Ahsan Ullah during a press conference at the university auditorium.
Protests escalated after the new VC entered the campus earlier in the day, reportedly accompanied by political activists, which the university community strongly condemned.
The associations alleged that two buses carrying students toward the campus from the city were attacked, demanding an immediate investigation and action against those responsible.
Professor Ahsan Ullah stated that the university community does not accept the new Vice-Chancellor and noted that 15 examinations have already been missed and classes have been suspended for 13 days.
Following the press conference, teachers held a procession on campus to further voice their demands for the reinstatement of former VC Professor Dr Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem.
caption:
Complete work abstention at CUET. Teachers and staff are demanding the removal of the new Vice-Chancellor.

Teachers, officers, and staff of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) have announced a complete work abstention and all-out non-cooperation to demand the removal of newly appointed Vice-Chancellor Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam.

The decision was announced by CUET Teachers’ Association President Professor Mohammad Ahsan Ullah during a press conference at the university auditorium.

Protests escalated after the new VC entered the campus earlier in the day, reportedly accompanied by political activists, which the university community strongly condemned.

The associations alleged that two buses carrying students toward the campus from the city were attacked, demanding an immediate investigation and action against those responsible.

Professor Ahsan Ullah stated that the university community does not accept the new Vice-Chancellor and noted that 15 examinations have already been missed and classes have been suspended for 13 days.

Following the press conference, teachers held a procession on campus to further voice their demands for the reinstatement of former VC Professor Dr Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem.

#CUET #UniversityProtest #Bangladesh #Education #AcademicCrisis

Source: The Daily Star, bdnews24.com, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV
